meta.title: Sentence Estimate Calculator (Sentencing Guidelines)
meta.description: Choose a crime, its type and the sentencing factors to see the recommended sentencing range (mitigated, basic or aggravated) under the 2026 Sentencing Guidelines, any special adjustment, and whether a suspended sentence is recommended.
meta.lead: Choose a crime and tick its type and the sentencing factors (the circumstances considered when deciding a sentence) to see the sentencing range the Sentencing Guidelines recommend and whether a suspended sentence is recommended.
meta.notice: This is a reference calculation based on the 2026 Sentencing Guidelines (Sentencing Commission). The guidelines are recommendations that judges refer to, and the actual sentence may differ. Which factors are recognized depends on the evidence and the circumstances of the case, so if you are facing trial, talk to a lawyer first.

form.typeDesc: Types are divided by the scale and result of the crime. Each type has a different basic sentencing range.
form.specialDesc: Special sentencing factors are the main circumstances that decide which range applies: mitigated, basic or aggravated. Conduct factors concern the crime itself; offender & other factors concern the defendant's circumstances and the like. Choose only the ones that apply.
form.generalDesc: These circumstances are considered when setting the exact sentence within the chosen range. They do not change the range, so they are not reflected in this calculation.
form.probationDesc: A suspended sentence (집행유예) means a prison sentence is imposed but not carried out for a set period; if that period passes without incident, the defendant does not serve the sentence. Major factors weigh more than general factors.
form.probationNegativeMajor: Major factors · toward a prison sentence (negative)
form.probationPositiveMajor: Major factors · toward a suspended sentence (positive)
form.probationNegativeGeneral: General factors · toward a prison sentence (negative)
form.probationPositiveGeneral: General factors · toward a suspended sentence (positive)
form.resultEmpty: Choose a type to see the recommended sentencing range. It is recalculated each time you choose a special sentencing factor.

rules.title: How the sentencing range is decided
items: Among special sentencing factors, those about the crime itself are called 'conduct factors', and those about the defendant's circumstances and the like are called 'offender & other factors'. When the numbers are equal, conduct factors weigh more. However, the victim not wanting punishment may be given the same weight as a conduct factor.
Factors of the same kind have the same weight.
If these two principles do not settle it, the judge compares all the factors and decides.
If the aggravating factors weigh more, the aggravated range is recommended; if the mitigating factors weigh more, the mitigated range; otherwise, the basic range.

In the aggravated range, if there are 2 or more special aggravating factors and no special mitigating factors, or special aggravating factors outnumber special mitigating factors by 2 or more, the upper limit of the range is raised by up to 1/2. In the mitigated range, in the opposite case, the lower limit is lowered by up to 1/2.

notes.title: Good to know
items: If several crimes were committed (concurrent crimes: several crimes not yet finally judged that are tried together), the range changes under the rules for multiple crimes. This calculation looks at only one crime.

If statutory mitigation or aggravation (voluntary surrender, repeat offense, etc.) changes the range of punishment available under the law (처단형), any part of the recommended range outside it is brought within its upper and lower limits.

The Sentencing Guidelines do not apply where a fine is chosen (except for election, traffic, stalking and animal protection crimes), to attempts (except attempted murder), to aiding and abetting, to defendants under 19, or where the crime is tried together with a crime already finally judged.

engine.mixed: {prison} in prison or a fine of {fine}
engine.weightNote: Factors that may be given the same weight as conduct factors, such as the victim not wanting punishment (or substantial repair of the harm), were counted as conduct factors.
engine.none: No special sentencing factors were chosen, so the Basic range applies.
engine.onlyAggravating: There are only special aggravating factors ({kinds}), so the aggravating factors weigh more.
engine.onlyMitigating: There are only special mitigating factors ({kinds}), so the mitigating factors weigh more.
engine.both: There are both aggravating factors ({agg}) and mitigating factors ({mit}).
engine.cancel: Factors of the same kind have the same weight, so equal numbers cancel each other out.
engine.even: Nothing is left after cancelling, so both sides weigh the same and the Basic range applies.
engine.aggravatingLeft: Only aggravating factors are left ({kinds}), so the aggravating factors weigh more.
engine.mitigatingLeft: Only mitigating factors are left ({kinds}), so the mitigating factors weigh more.
engine.remainLeft: What remains: {a} conduct factor(s) on the {actSide} side and {r} offender & other factor(s) on the {actorSide} side.
engine.remainHave: There are {a} conduct factor(s) on the {actSide} side and {r} offender & other factor(s) on the {actorSide} side.
engine.sameNumber: With equal numbers, conduct factors weigh more than offender & other factors, so the {side} side weighs more.
engine.moreAct: The conduct factors are both more numerous and heavier, so the {side} side weighs more.
engine.undecided: Conduct factors are heavier, but offender & other factors are more numerous, so these principles alone do not decide which side weighs more. In this case, the judge compares all the factors and decides.
engine.undecidedZone: Depending on which side the judge finds heavier, the Mitigated range or the Aggravated range applies; if they are about equal, the Basic range applies. In this case, special adjustment does not follow automatically even if the factors differ by 2 or more.
engine.altZone: Treating the victim not wanting punishment, etc. the same as a conduct factor is the judge's choice. If counted as an offender & other factor instead, the result would be: {zone}.
engine.upperOnly: In the Aggravated range there are only special aggravating factors ({n}), so the upper limit can be raised by up to 1/2.
engine.upperMore: In the Aggravated range there are {n} more special aggravating factors than special mitigating factors, so the upper limit can be raised by up to 1/2.
engine.upperNone: {reason} However, this range has no fixed upper limit, so it does not change.
engine.lowerOnly: In the Mitigated range there are only special mitigating factors ({n}), so the lower limit can be lowered by up to 1/2.
engine.lowerMore: In the Mitigated range there are {n} more special mitigating factors than special aggravating factors, so the lower limit can be lowered by up to 1/2.
engine.lowerNone: {reason} However, this range has no fixed lower limit, so it does not change.
engine.probationJudge: Decided by the judge's overall assessment
engine.probationCounts: Major factors: {pm} positive, {nm} negative · General factors: {pg} positive, {ng} negative
engine.suspendOverruled: There are {major} more major positive factors, but general negative factors outnumber general positive factors by {opp}, a larger difference. In this case, the judge compares all the factors and decides.
engine.suspendOnly: There are only major positive factors ({n}), so a suspended sentence is recommended.
engine.suspendMore: There are {n} more major positive factors than major negative factors, so a suspended sentence is recommended.
engine.prisonOverruled: There are {major} more major negative factors, but general positive factors outnumber general negative factors by {opp}, a larger difference. In this case, the judge compares all the factors and decides.
engine.prisonOnly: There are only major negative factors ({n}), so a prison sentence is recommended.
engine.prisonMore: There are {n} more major negative factors than major positive factors, so a prison sentence is recommended.
engine.judgeMajor: The difference in major factors is less than 2, so the judge compares all the suspended sentence factors and decides. Even then, major factors weigh more than general factors.
